root_cause.pre_fix_behavior: A canonical owner handoff/review outcome or assignment mismatch immediately called terminate_worker_pid, then published worker completion or supersession. Governance lifecycle movement was treated as execution-lease cancellation.

scope.owned_layer: Active worker governance-transition classification, exact process-generation termination, worker-status audit provenance, and supervisor/ai-status regressions.
scope.not_changing: Account or quota groups, configured identity equivalence, reviewer policy, provider configuration, live runtime/services, deployment, product tasks, or canonical state by hand.

contract.process_generation: One deterministic SHA-256 identity binds schema version, task ID, worker run ID, queue event ID, PID, and Linux /proc starttime ticks.
contract.signal_boundary: Termination signals are sent only after the stored process generation validates and current /proc starttime equals the captured starttime; PID reuse or unreadable identity fails closed.
contract.governance_preservation: Assign, start, progress, note, reopen, handoff, review approval, and ordinary review/finalize lifecycle movement do not cancel a healthy lease.
contract.authorized_termination: Configured terminal task truth, valid explicit cancel/supersession activity, exact supervisor task_reassigned evidence, or existing eligible priority preemption may end the exact process generation.
contract.canonical_order: The recent validated canonical activity tail is consumed in append order and the latest task transition after lease acquisition controls assignment evidence.
contract.concurrency: Missing, invalid, stale, or assignment-divergent evidence preserves the worker; a later cycle can decide from fresh canonical truth.
contract.lock_boundary: When the runtime admission lock is held, an exact termination is queued and the worker remains nonterminal until identity-bound confirmation runs after lock release.
contract.audit_separation: Worker execution identity, status-command producer lease, review provenance, task lifecycle, governance decision, and termination reason are recorded as separate fields/events.
contract.identity_policy: Codex and Codex2 remain distinct configured identities/quota groups and may review one another; no policy/config change is introduced.

incident_exit_143_reproduced.evidence: Two immutable runner-status files record signal 15 / exit 143 after the 09:45 and 09:49-09:50 governed handoffs.
